description: Seed corpus for the Nadobro knowledge hub. Consumed by the Phase-6 ingestion pipeline; curated for THIS bot's job — market making and grid strategies on a thin perpetual CLOB — not as a general trading reading list.

tiers.peer_reviewed: Published or preprint research. May inform feature design and be cited in user-facing explanations.
tiers.practitioner: Working professionals and production systems. Credible mechanism, weaker evidence. Hypothesis source.
tiers.reference: Canonical textbooks and documentation. Definitional ground truth.
tiers.retail_unverified: Retail education. Ingested ONLY as a hypothesis source. Concepts from this tier must be formalized as a quant/structure.py feature and beat baseline in backtest before touching any parameter.

policy.prose_cannot_set_parameters: No tier, including peer_reviewed, may change a live trading parameter directly. Prose proposes; quant/scoring.py and the backtest harness dispose.
policy.ingestible: false means the pipeline cannot fetch it (paywall, print). Listed because it is worth a human reading, and because its concepts are referenced by ingestible sources.

sources.title: The Price Impact of Order Book Events
sources.why: Order flow imbalance is near-linearly related to short-horizon price change, with slope inversely proportional to depth. This is the core formula for the Phase-5 adverse-selection defense and it is only computable now that Phase 1 populates real book sizes. The depth-scaling term matters especially on Nado: the same imbalance is far more potent on a thin book.

sources.title: Funding-Aware Optimal Market Making for Perpetual DEXs
sources.why: The closest published match to Nadobro's exact problem: stochastic-control market making on a perpetual DEX where funding payments enter the objective. Conclusion is directly actionable — spreads should widen when funding penalizes the inventory you are accumulating. Mid mode currently ignores funding entirely when quoting.

sources.title: High-frequency trading in a limit order book
sources.why: The canonical inventory-aware quoting model: reservation price shifts away from inventory, spread widens with volatility and risk aversion. Mid mode's spread logic is a fixed percentage with a bias skew — this is the principled replacement, and the inventory-skew term is the direct fix for the 'MM bleeds in trends' failure.

sources.title: Dealing with the inventory risk: a solution to the market making problem
sources.why: Reduces Avellaneda-Stoikov to closed-form asymptotic quotes with explicit inventory bounds. This is the tractable version an event-loop bot can actually evaluate per tick without solving a PDE.

sources.title: Queuing and inventories in limit order markets
sources.why: Treats queue position and inventory risk jointly rather than separately. Nadobro already has queue-preservation logic (_holds_queue_position / _should_hold in market_making.py); this is the theory that says when holding queue is worth the adverse-selection cost.

sources.title: Market Microstructure Knowledge Needed for Controlling an Intra-Day Trading Process
sources.why: The practitioner's map of what actually drives intraday execution quality. Open-access and broad — good backbone for the hub's microstructure section.

sources.title: Adaptive Optimal Market Making Strategies with Inventory Liquidation Costs
sources.why: Prices in the cost of unwinding inventory, not just holding it. On a thin venue the exit cost dominates, which is precisely why Nadobro's MM can look profitable on paper and lose on the flatten.

sources.title: Market Making under a Weakly Consistent Limit Order Book Model
sources.why: Market making without assuming a well-behaved book — the realistic regime for a young L2 CLOB where depth is sparse and intermittent.

sources.title: Optimal liquidity-based trading tactics
sources.why: When to post passive versus cross the spread, as a function of available liquidity. Directly relevant to the standing maker-first rule and to the vol bot's taker legs.

sources.title: Optimal Execution of Limit and Market Orders with Trade Director, Speed Limiter, and Fill Uncertainty
sources.why: Fill uncertainty is the thing that breaks naive ladder planning: a rung that never fills is not free, it is unhedged intent. Relevant to quant/ladder.py sizing.

sources.title: Asymmetric statistics of order books: the role of discreteness and evidence for strategic order placement
sources.why: Tick discreteness and strategic placement shape where liquidity actually sits. Nadobro joins/improves the touch by one tick; this is the evidence on whether that is the right rule.

sources.title: Market impact with multi-timescale liquidity
sources.why: Liquidity replenishes on multiple timescales, so impact is not a single number. Matters for sizing grid rungs on a venue where a single order can move the book.

sources.title: Dynamic Modeling of Limit Order Book and Market Maker Strategy Optimization Based on Markov Queue Theory
sources.why: Open-access queue-theoretic treatment of book dynamics and MM policy. Useful as an implementable bridge between theory and the depth feed.

sources.title: ClusterLOB: Enhancing Trading Strategies by Clustering Orders in Limit Order Books
sources.why: Separating order flow by participant behavior is the rigorous version of what retail calls 'smart money'. If any part of the SMC narrative is real, this is the shape it takes in the literature.

sources.title: Perpetual Futures Pricing
sources.why: The arbitrage-pricing foundation for the instrument Nadobro actually trades. Establishes which funding specifications tether perp to spot — necessary background for the delta-neutral strategy and for reading funding as a signal rather than a fee.

sources.title: Designing funding rates for perpetual futures
sources.why: Models funding as an algorithmic feedback rule producing an endogenously mean-reverting basis. If basis mean-reverts by construction, that is a tradeable structural property rather than a forecast — the strongest available edge for delta-neutral.

sources.title: The Two-Tiered Structure of Cryptocurrency Funding Rate Markets
sources.why: Open-access empirical study of how funding behaves across venues. Context for whether Nado's funding is idiosyncratic or tracks the broader market.

sources.title: Exploring risk and return profiles of funding rate arbitrage on CEX and DEX
sources.why: The sobering number: only ~40% of top funding-arb opportunities stay positive after transaction costs and spread reversal. A direct warning for how delta-neutral should size and gate, and evidence that fee-aware backtesting is not optional.

sources.title: The Deflated Sharpe Ratio: Correcting for Selection Bias, Backtest Overfitting and Non-Normality
sources.why: The gate that stops the nightly hypothesis loop from fooling itself. Once the loop tries many variants per night, an undeflated Sharpe is meaningless — the number of trials must be priced in before any weight is promoted out of shadow mode.

sources.title: Pseudo-Mathematics and Financial Charlatanism / Statistical Overfitting and Backtest Performance
sources.authors: Bailey, Borwein, Lopez de Prado, Zhu
sources.why: Quantifies how few trials it takes to manufacture a beautiful backtest from noise. This is the paper that justifies the shadow-mode requirement and the minimum graded-sample floor in quant/scoring.py.

sources.title: Determining Optimal Trading Rules without Backtesting
sources.why: Derives profit-taking and stop-loss levels analytically from the process rather than by grid-searching a backtest. Directly applicable to choosing SL/TP defaults per strategy instead of tuning them into overfit.

sources.title: Most claimed statistical findings in cross-sectional return predictability are likely true
sources.why: The counterweight to blanket replication-crisis pessimism. Keeps the loop from discarding real effects out of excessive skepticism — the failure mode opposite to overfitting.

sources.title: Time Series Momentum
sources.why: The best-evidenced directional effect in existence: own past return predicts future return across 58 instruments and 25 years. Relevant because it is the thing that KILLS grid strategies — a persistent trend is exactly the regime in which a grid accumulates one-sided losses. R-Grid is already trend-following; this is the evidence base for that choice.

sources.title: Market Regime Detection using Hidden Markov Models
sources.why: Worked implementation of regime detection feeding regime-specialized models. Nadobro's variance-ratio and volume-profile gates are hand-rolled classifiers; this is the standard alternative to benchmark them against.

sources.title: Why grid and martingale systems quietly destroy accounts
sources.why: The single most relevant failure literature for this product. Grids win small ~99% of the time and can lose everything in one trending day; the strategy is only unconditionally solvent with infinite capital. Nadobro ships three grid variants to real users, so the structural failure mode must be modeled explicitly, not discovered live.

sources.title: Building a Research-Grounded Grid EA: Why Most Grid EAs Fail
sources.why: Catalogs the concrete failure causes — undercapitalization, poor pair selection, running through trends — in a form that maps onto specific Nadobro config gates.

sources.title: Fractional Kelly and risk of ruin in practice
sources.why: Full Kelly is not survivable when the edge is estimated rather than known, and Nadobro's edge will always be estimated — from quant/scoring.py, with error bars. Professionals run 25-50% Kelly. This bounds how aggressive the Phase-4 conviction multiplier may ever become.

sources.title: Sizing the Risk: Kelly, VIX, and Hybrid Approaches
sources.why: Blends Kelly with volatility state — size up in calm, down in stress. The formal version of what the conviction multiplier should be doing, and a check that it never scales up into a volatility spike.

sources.title: Hummingbot Documentation
sources.why: The most mature open-source crypto market-making framework, and the direct ancestor of Nadobro's engine vocabulary — controllers, executors, position/DCA/grid/TWAP building blocks. The closest thing to a spec for the architecture already in this repo.

sources.title: Hummingbot source
sources.why: Reference implementations of the same strategy families Nadobro runs. Read for the edge cases their issue tracker has already found.

sources.title: awesome-systematic-trading
sources.why: Curated index of libraries and papers; useful as a discovery feed for the hub rather than as content itself.

sources.title: arXiv q-fin.TR (Trading and Market Microstructure) — recent
sources.why: The primary daily feed for this bot's actual domain. Note arXiv is preprint, not peer-reviewed — tier reflects venue quality, not review status, so anything acted upon still needs the backtest gate.

sources.title: QuantPedia blog
sources.why: Extracts explicit trading rules and performance characteristics from academic papers — already in the formalized shape the hypothesis loop requires. Their crypto section reviews 20+ equity anomalies tested on daily crypto data, with momentum the strongest survivor.

sources.title: QuantPedia cryptocurrency trading research
sources.why: Crypto-specific anomaly replication. The place to check whether an effect claimed in equities survives in this asset class before formalizing it as a feature.

sources.title: Charles-Albert Lehalle — publications
sources.why: One of the few researchers publishing continuously on exactly this intersection — optimal quoting, adverse selection, queue-reactive book models. Worth tracking as an author feed rather than paper by paper.

sources.title: Trading and Exchanges: Market Microstructure for Practitioners
sources.why: The foundational text. Explains WHO trades and WHY — informed traders, liquidity suppliers, and the structure of the losses a market maker takes. Read before assuming any pattern-based edge exists.

sources.title: Trades, Quotes and Prices: Financial Markets Under the Microscope
sources.why: The empirical laws of order books — impact, order flow autocorrelation, liquidity dynamics. The best single source for what a book actually does, as opposed to what models assume.

sources.title: Market Microstructure in Practice (2nd ed.)
sources.why: Bridges microstructure theory to what desks actually run, including liquidity attrition and fragmentation.

sources.title: Systematic Trading
sources.why: The design philosophy behind Phase 4: continuous forecasts scaled to conviction rather than binary on/off, capped at a bounded range, with overfitting treated as the primary enemy. Forecasts near zero are demonstrably less profitable than strong ones — which is exactly why the conviction score must be continuous.

sources.title: Investment Idiocy (Rob Carver)
sources.why: Ongoing, unusually honest working notes on forecast construction, position sizing and what fails. Free and ingestible, unlike the book.

sources.title: Advances in Financial Machine Learning
sources.why: Labeling, sample weighting, cross-validation that respects time, and the mechanics of not fooling yourself. The methodological spine for the grading loop.

sources.title: Mind Over Markets (auction market theory / Market Profile)
sources.why: The rigorous ancestor of everything SMC gestures at: value area, point of control, and acceptance versus rejection tested by price, time and volume. Maps directly onto volume_profile() already in regime_gate.py, and gives the falsifiable definition of a real breakout versus a false one.

sources.title: The ULTIMATE Smart Money Concepts Guide (full SMC course)
sources.why: HYPOTHESIS SOURCE ONLY. The phenomena it names — stop clustering at obvious swing highs/lows, sweeps, failed breakouts — are real and formalizable. The narrative around them (order blocks as distinct entities, accumulation/manipulation/distribution, precise Fibonacci entries) has no rigorous support and is too discretionary to backtest as taught. Concepts may become quant/structure.py features; they may never set a parameter.

sources.title: Smart Money Concepts — statistical review
sources.why: The counterweight that must be ingested alongside any SMC material: separates the documented phenomena from the unsupported narrative. Keeps the hypothesis loop honest about which retail concepts have any evidence behind them.
